meta.name: Build an enterprise deal knowledge graph with Salesforce, Gmail and Neo4j

parameters.name: statement
parameters.value:
=UNWIND $nodes AS node
CALL {
  WITH node

  FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN node.type = 'contact' THEN [1] ELSE [] END |
    MERGE (n:Contact {id: node.id})
    SET n.name = coalesce(node.name, ''),
        n.email = coalesce(node.email, ''),
        n.display_name = coalesce(node.display_name, coalesce(node.name, '')),
        n.engagement_score = coalesce(node.engagement_score, 0),
        n.stakeholder_role_hint = coalesce(node.stakeholder_role_hint, ''),
        n.latest_interaction_at = node.latest_interaction_at,
        n.open_pipeline_amount = coalesce(node.open_pipeline_amount, 0),
        n.email_count = coalesce(node.email_count, 0),
        n.meeting_count = coalesce(node.meeting_count, 0),
        n.opportunity_count = coalesce(node.opportunity_count, 0)
  )

  FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN node.type = 'account' THEN [1] ELSE [] END |
    MERGE (n:Account {id: node.id})
    SET n.name = coalesce(node.name, ''),
        n.display_name = coalesce(node.display_name, coalesce(node.name, '')),
        n.account_type = coalesce(node.account_type, 'Unknown'),
        n.account_key = coalesce(node.account_key, ''),
        n.total_contacts = coalesce(node.total_contacts, 0),
        n.total_opportunities = coalesce(node.total_opportunities, 0),
        n.total_open_pipeline = coalesce(node.total_open_pipeline, 0),
        n.total_weighted_pipeline = coalesce(node.total_weighted_pipeline, 0),
        n.total_email_count = coalesce(node.total_email_count, 0),
        n.total_meeting_count = coalesce(node.total_meeting_count, 0),
        n.latest_interaction_at = node.latest_interaction_at
  )

  FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN node.type = 'opportunity' THEN [1] ELSE [] END |
    MERGE (n:Opportunity {id: node.id})
    SET n.name = coalesce(node.name, ''),
        n.display_name = coalesce(node.display_name, coalesce(node.name, '')),
        n.amount = coalesce(node.amount, 0),
        n.probability = coalesce(node.probability, 0),
        n.weighted_amount = coalesce(node.weighted_amount, 0),
        n.opportunity_type = coalesce(node.opportunity_type, 'Unknown Opportunity Type')
  )

  FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN node.type = 'email' THEN [1] ELSE [] END |
    MERGE (n:Email {id: node.id})
    SET n.subject = coalesce(node.subject, 'No Subject'),
        n.display_name = coalesce(node.display_name, coalesce(node.subject, 'No Subject')),
        n.timestamp = node.timestamp,
        n.from_email = coalesce(node.from_email, ''),
        n.to_emails = coalesce(node.to_emails, []),
        n.cc_emails = coalesce(node.cc_emails, []),
        n.snippet = coalesce(node.snippet, '')
  )

  FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN node.type = 'meeting' THEN [1] ELSE [] END |
    MERGE (n:Meeting {id: node.id})
    SET n.title = coalesce(node.title, 'Untitled Meeting'),
        n.display_name = coalesce(node.display_name, coalesce(node.title, 'Untitled Meeting')),
        n.start_time = node.start_time,
        n.end_time = node.end_time,
        n.organizer_email = coalesce(node.organizer_email, ''),
        n.attendee_emails = coalesce(node.attendee_emails, []),
        n.status = coalesce(node.status, ''),
        n.location = coalesce(node.location, '')
  )

  RETURN 1 AS done
}
RETURN size($nodes) AS nodes_processed

parameters.name: statement
parameters.value:
=UNWIND $edges AS edge
MATCH (from {id: edge.from})
MATCH (to {id: edge.to})

FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN edge.relation = 'BELONGS_TO' THEN [1] ELSE [] END |
  MERGE (from)-[r:BELONGS_TO]->(to)
)

FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN edge.relation = 'INVOLVED_IN' THEN [1] ELSE [] END |
  MERGE (from)-[r:INVOLVED_IN]->(to)
  SET r.amount = coalesce(edge.amount, 0),
      r.probability = coalesce(edge.probability, 0),
      r.weighted_amount = coalesce(edge.weighted_amount, 0),
      r.opportunity_type = coalesce(edge.opportunity_type, 'Unknown Opportunity Type')
)

FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN edge.relation = 'OWNS' THEN [1] ELSE [] END |
  MERGE (from)-[r:OWNS]->(to)
  SET r.amount = coalesce(edge.amount, 0),
      r.probability = coalesce(edge.probability, 0),
      r.weighted_amount = coalesce(edge.weighted_amount, 0),
      r.opportunity_type = coalesce(edge.opportunity_type, 'Unknown Opportunity Type')
)

FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN edge.relation = 'SENT_OR_RECEIVED' THEN [1] ELSE [] END |
  MERGE (from)-[r:SENT_OR_RECEIVED]->(to)
  SET r.timestamp = edge.timestamp,
      r.subject = coalesce(edge.subject, 'No Subject')
)

FOREACH (_ IN CASE WHEN edge.relation = 'ATTENDED' THEN [1] ELSE [] END |
  MERGE (from)-[r:ATTENDED]->(to)
  SET r.start_time = edge.start_time,
      r.end_time = edge.end_time,
      r.status = coalesce(edge.status, '')
)

RETURN size($edges) AS edges_processed

parameters.content:
**Title: Enterprise Deal Knowledge Graph Builder — Overview**

This workflow aggregates enterprise data from Salesforce, Gmail, and Google Calendar to build a unified relationship intelligence graph in Neo4j. It runs on a scheduled trigger and begins by fetching contacts, accounts, opportunities, emails, and meeting data. Each dataset is normalized into a consistent structure, ensuring clean and usable records.

Next, the workflow combines all data sources and builds contact-centric relationship profiles. These profiles include engagement metrics such as email activity, meeting frequency, opportunity involvement, and calculated engagement scores. Based on these enriched profiles, a graph payload is constructed with nodes (Contact, Account, Opportunity, Email, Meeting) and relationships between them.

Finally, the workflow writes structured nodes and relationships into Neo4j, enabling advanced querying and visualization of deal pipelines and stakeholder interactions.

**Setup Steps:**

1. Configure credentials for Salesforce, Gmail, Google Calendar, and Neo4j
2. Update values in **Set Workflow Config**
3. Test each data node individually
4. Run the full workflow once
5. Activate **Enterprise Data Aggregation Scheduler**

## Section: Data Sources ##

Fetches raw data from:

* Get Salesforce Contacts
* Get Salesforce Accounts
* Get Salesforce Opportunities
* Get Gmail Messages
* Get Calendar Events

Build Gmail Query From Contacts dynamically filters Gmail data.

## Section: Normalization & Profiling

Normalizes all datasets using:

* Normalize Contacts / Accounts / Opportunities
* Normalize Emails / Meetings

Aggregate All Data Sources merges inputs.
Build Contact Relationship Profiles creates engagement metrics and unified profiles.

## Section: Graph Builder & Storage

Builds and stores the knowledge graph:

* Build Graph Payload creates nodes and edges
* Write Nodes To Neo4j stores entities
* Write Relationships To Neo4j connects relationships

Creates a fully connected Neo4j graph for analysis.
